sentences.text: In AC circuits with inductors and capacitors, voltage and current are out of phase.
Real Power P, measured in Watts, is the actual power converted into useful work and heat: P = Vrms × Irms × cos(theta).
Reactive Power Q, measured in VAR, is the power bouncing between the source and reactive fields: Q = Vrms × Irms × sin(theta).
Apparent Power S, measured in Volt-Amps (VA), is the vector combination: S = sqrt(P squared + Q squared).
The Power Factor is cos(theta) = P / S. Power Factor Correction: Industrial electric motors draw inductive reactive power ( +Q L ).
Utilities penalize factories with low power factors ( PF Capacitor Banks ( -Q C ) cancels out lagging VARs, raising PF approaches 1.0 without changing real active work ( P ).
